label: de_morgan
graph_version: 3.9.8 (3.9.7 + one primary per misconception (S9c) and the four remaining sibling edges (S9b), 2026-11-04; listed in revision_3_9_8)

edges.label:
[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: 'not (A and B)' is read as 'not A and not B', the way a minus sign is distributed over a sum in algebra without changing the operator. Java (Boolean logic) rule: negating a compound condition negates each term and also flips && to || (and || to &&).
[1] misconception (M) -> NegationDistributesUnchanged: wrong rule: !(a && b) is the same as !a && !b. Right rule: !(a && b) is !a || !b, and !(a || b) is !a && !b (De Morgan); !a && !b differs whenever exactly one of a, b is true.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> NegationDistributesUnchanged: Points to LT (push ! into every term, replace each relation by its opposite, and swap && and ||, all together). Applied unevenly: the student negates the terms but keeps the operator, or turns !(x < 5) into x > 5 instead of x >= 5 in one term while handling the other correctly. (here mixing in: "!(a && b) is the same as !a && !b")

[0] names_the_element (N): De Morgan's laws are rules of Boolean logic that show how to negate a logical expression.
[1] states_the_rule (S): !(A && B) is equivalent to !A || !B, and !(A || B) is equivalent to !A && !B; with comparisons, negating a term uses the opposite relational operator (!(x < 5) is x >= 5).

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): As a rewrite: move the ! inside the parentheses, negate each term (flipping each comparison), swap && and ||; as evaluation, both forms give the same value on every row of the truth table and short-circuit after the same left operand.
[1] output_prediction (OP): The rewritten expression has the same boolean value as the original for all inputs: with x = 1 and y = 0, !(x == 0 || y == 0) and x != 0 && y != 0 are both false.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Rewriting changes no program state; both forms evaluate the same terms in the same left-to-right order, so side effects and short-circuit points are unchanged.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): De Morgan's laws relate the three logical operators: a negated && becomes an || of negations and a negated || becomes an && of negations.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Used to simplify negated conditions into readable positive ones, e.g. turning a stopping condition ('found or at the end') into a loop-continuation condition while (!found && i < n), or simplifying (!(a < b) && !(a > b)) to a == b.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> NegationDistributesUnchanged: A correct De Morgan rewrite preserves the value for every input (invariant); dropping the operator flip, or using > instead of >= for !(x < 5), breaks it exactly on mixed or boundary inputs.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Apply De Morgan when a condition is written as !(...) of a compound, or when converting a 'stop when' condition into a 'continue while' condition; leave a condition alone when its positive form is already clear.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Negation flips && and || (De Morgan). Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Inputs where exactly one term is true (and boundary values of negated comparisons) after a condition was negated term by term without flipping the operator.
wrong: !(a && b) is the same as !a && !b. | right: !(a && b) is !a || !b (De Morgan).
De Morgan's laws rewrite expressions built from && , || and !.
